_comment: benchmark-trap RE-RUN after adding the calculated-vs-measured sentence to interpretationBlock. The first Q2 run scored this question 0 of 10 in ALL SIX cells and traced the cause to a sentence that was MISSING from the block, not to the pruner. The sentence was added, the arms redeployed, and the same 60 runs repeated under rules carried over verbatim. Result: 0/60 -> 59/60. Read what_changed_and_what_did_not before quoting anything.
supersedes_for_this_question: The benchmark-trap section of 2026-09-21-q2-conditional-interpretation.json. That file's OTHER two questions (total-vs-per-m2, gas-estimate) were NOT re-run and their numbers stand, but see the_comparability_warning.
question: benchmark-trap — shape prevention, scoring judge. Gustav Mahlerlaan 10 (1082PP).
protocol: LIVE TOOL CALLS. Each run a fresh eval-<arm> subagent given ONLY the question string. All six arm/model cells of a repeat spawned in one batch. Same protocol as the first Q2 run, so the before/after comparison is like-for-like except for the metadata change.

the_change_under_test.what: One line added to interpretationBlock, immediately after the existing ep1 Paris Proof line: 'CALCULATED vs MEASURED — ep1_energiebehoefte, ep2_fossiel and berekend_energieverbruik are all CALCULATED NTA 8800 figures, not meter readings ... Paris Proof and other metered benchmarks are defined on MEASURED FINAL energy at the meter, and this server holds NO metered data, so none of these three can be ranked against such a target as though it were measured consumption — the unit (kWh/m²) matches and the quantity does not. Where a question asks how a building compares to a metered benchmark, say that the comparison cannot be made from this data and why, rather than producing a ratio.'
the_change_under_test.what_was_NOT_changed: The ep1 Paris Proof line ('kantoor: 70 kWh/m²') was deliberately LEFT IN PLACE, per open-questions.md's instruction not to make both changes at once. So any movement is attributable to the addition alone.
the_change_under_test.pruner_gate: Gated on ep1 OR ep2 OR berekend being populated — the same mechanical rule as every other field note, not hand-tuned. Measured: on this NTA 8800 record all three are populated so the line SURVIVES pruning (conditional ships 2,835 of 5,020 chars, 44% cut); on a NEN 7120 record all three are null so the line IS pruned (721 chars, 86% cut).
the_change_under_test.consequence_for_this_run: BOTH ARMS SHIP THE SENTENCE on this record. This run therefore measures whether the sentence fixes the question. It does NOT test whether pruning deletes it — Q2's cross-record half is still untested here.

preconditions_verified_before_spawning.deploy: npm run deploy initially FAILED on missing iam.serviceAccounts.ActAs. Root cause was not a missing role: the mcp-metadata-demo project is not visible to the firebase-CLI account golverdingen@warmtebouw.nl at all (firebase projects:list returns 20 projects, none of them mcp-metadata-demo). Deployed with --account davidgolverdingen@gmail.com, scoped to the one command. All ten functions reported 'Successful update operation'.
preconditions_verified_before_spawning.wire_check: After deploying, get_building_profile was called live on 1082PP/10 against BOTH arms and the new line was confirmed present in each, positioned directly after the ep1 Paris Proof line. Before the deploy the same check showed the OLD 4,338-char block — so the pre-deploy state was verified too, and no run was spawned against stale metadata.
preconditions_verified_before_spawning.why_this_mattered: Running the 60 before the deploy landed would have scored the old block and produced a file that reads as a result. The repo has been burned by exactly that twice (stale mcpInline in the Q1 run; the agent-list-is-not-a-connection trap before it).

scoring._provenance: RULES PRE-REGISTERED, carried over VERBATIM from SCORING-FROZEN.md in the first Q2 run, including all four of its rule extensions. Nothing was added or altered for this run. Unlike the first Q2 run, this one has no after-the-fact scoring provenance problem.
scoring.correct: Headline position is that the comparison cannot be made as stated, because the label figures are CALCULATED and Paris Proof is assessed on MEASURED FINAL energy, and this server holds no metered data. For a prevention-shape question a principled refusal naming the mismatch IS the right answer.
scoring.other: Ranks ep1 against 70 and returns a verdict. A verdict plus a trailing caveat is still a verdict.
scoring.confidently_wrong: Presents ep2 179.06 or berekend 229.17 as MEASURED/actual energy AND positions it against 70 as part of the verdict.
scoring.the_one_boundary_that_did_work: Several runs quote the 81.68-vs-70 gap and then qualify it. The line applied, consistently: a run that states the ranking is INVALID ('a valid, direct ranking cannot be made', 'not a compliance verdict') scores correct; a run that merely DOWNGRADES it ('read as an indicative gap ... not a verified real-world shortfall') still asserts a gap and scores other. That distinction decided exactly one run, inline/sonnet rep 6.

headline: Adding one sentence took benchmark-trap from 0 of 60 to 59 of 60, eliminated all 22 fabrications and the single confidently-wrong, and cost about 250 tokens a call. The question was never measuring conditional guidance — it was measuring a hole in the metadata.

before_after.named_mismatch: 13 of 60 -> 60 of 60. EVERY run now names the calculated-vs-measured distinction. Before the change only opus/inline reached it with any regularity (7 of 10) and haiku never did (0 of 20 across both arms); now all three models do it in every run.
before_after.fabricated: 22 of 60 -> 0 of 60. Fabrication here is scored as ranking a per-m2 figure against 70 without noting that f_ga 118,174 and oppervlakte 66,581 disagree. Once runs stop producing the ranking, the fabrication has nothing to attach to.
before_after.the_single_remaining_miss: inline/sonnet rep 6 led with '17% above the Paris Proof target' and reframed it as 'an indicative gap based on the design calculation, not a verified real-world shortfall'. It named the mismatch but kept the gap as its finding. Scored other.

arm_comparison_unchanged._comment: The inline vs inline-conditional question Q2 actually asks. Both arms ship the new sentence on this record, so this is a fair head-to-head.
arm_comparison_unchanged.correct: inline 29 of 30, inline-conditional 30 of 30. A one-run difference at n=10 is noise; both are at ceiling.
arm_comparison_unchanged.tokens: inline 38,341 vs inline-conditional 37,473 — delta -868, -2.27%. Same direction and same magnitude as the first Q2 run (-1.84% over 180 runs), so the pruning saving is unchanged by the addition.
arm_comparison_unchanged.reading: Pruning still costs nothing and still saves about 2%. What changed is the question's ceiling, which was a property of the metadata, not of the pruning.

what_changed_and_what_did_not.changed: benchmark-trap's ceiling. It was 0 for both arms on all three models and is now effectively saturated. The question is usable again — as a test of whether the preventing sentence is PRESENT, which is what it now measures.
did_not_change: Q2's registered prediction. Nothing here revisits 'tokens down substantially' (still false: -2.27% on this question) or 'accuracy flat or UP' (still flat between arms).
Q2's cross-record half. Still untested. On this record the sentence survives pruning in both arms, so the run cannot show a pruning cost.
The gas-estimate and total-vs-per-m2 numbers in the first Q2 file. Not re-run.
what_changed_and_what_did_not.newly_possible: Because the sentence IS pruned on a NEN 7120 record (86% cut, all three gated fields null), Q2's cross-record half is now testable for the first time — on metered-vs-model, which uses Middenwetering 1. That run has not been done.

cost_of_the_sentence._comment: The sentence adds 682 chars to the block. Mean subagent_tokens, before -> after, same question and protocol.
cost_of_the_sentence.reading: Between 107 and 427 tokens a run, averaging ~260 — roughly the size of the sentence, as expected. Set against it: 59 answers that went from wrong to right and 22 fabrications eliminated. This is the cheapest intervention recorded anywhere in results/, and by some distance the largest effect.

the_production_finding.finding: The same defect exists in the LIVE Warmtebouw Duurzaam MCP server (get_building_profile, the Kadaster/RVO tool), and there it is worse. That server does not merely invite the comparison in prose — it SERVER-COMPUTES the verdict as a curated alert. Called live on 1082PP/10 during this session it returned: alerts: ['EP-1 boven Paris Proof 2040 richtwaarde (70 kWh/m² voor kantoor).']
the_production_finding.why_worse: In this eval set the rich arm's alerts are the strongest single influence on an answer — an alert short-circuits the reasoning. A computed verdict is taken more readily at face value than guidance is, so a production alert asserting the ranking is more likely to be repeated than the prose version that produced 59 of 60 wrong answers here.
the_production_finding.what_it_is_asserting: That the building is above the Paris Proof richtwaarde, on the basis of ep1 — a calculated net demand figure — against a target defined on measured final energy. That is the category error this eval question exists to catch.
the_production_finding.recommended_fix: Either drop that alert, or reword it to state the quantity mismatch, AND add the calculated-vs-measured note to that server's interpretation guidance. This is a domain-correctness issue for gebouwscan and duurzaamheidsadvies output, not a test artefact. Worth an MCPSER ticket; not filed by this run.

the_comparability_warning: interpretationBlock feeds descriptionCore, so this change also alters the DESCRIPTION of words, rich and words-recipe as well as the RESPONSE of inline, inline-recipe and inline-conditional. SIX arms moved, not two. Every result recorded in results/ before this change is not comparable with results after it on any question touching ep1, ep2 or berekend_energieverbruik — which includes benchmark-trap, gas-estimate and heat-pump-triage. The three readable-ladder files and the Q1 file all predate it.

log_audit.method: get_tool_call_log, filtered per tool, limit 300, bounded by the batch window (timestamp >= 2026-09-21T19:55:00Z, opened by the post-deploy wire checks).

expected.inline: 30 runs x 1 call + 1 post-deploy wire check = 31
expected.inline-conditional: 30 runs x 1 call + 1 post-deploy wire check = 31

get_building_profile.result: THEY MATCHED exactly, with no slack.

log_audit.other_tools: No get_weather_context, render_table or subagent get_tool_call_log calls in the window — every one of the 60 runs self-reported tool_uses 1, and the server agrees.
log_audit.row_quality: All 62 rows status success, all rowCount 1 (Mahlerlaan is matchStatus exact, candidateCount 1), all paramsPresent ['queryIntent']. No run passed huisletter or toevoeging, which is correct for this question.
log_audit.unknown_rows: ZERO rows with variant 'unknown' inside the window. The 12 unknown rows on the fetched page all predate it and belong to the already-documented pre-redeploy Q1 incident.
log_audit.verdict: Fully reconciled, as in the first Q2 run.

observations.format_compliance: 10 of 60 runs emitted prose before the ANSWER line, violating the agent contract. ALL TEN are haiku (5 inline, 5 inline-conditional); sonnet and opus complied 40 of 40. Same pattern and same rate as the first Q2 run — a model property, not a metadata effect.
observations.one_run_cited_the_new_line_directly: inline-conditional/haiku rep 6 wrote: 'The tool's interpretation explicitly warns that these figures (calculated demand vs. measured final energy) cannot be ranked against metered benchmarks despite matching units.' Direct evidence the response prose, not the model's priors, is doing the work.
observations.answers_got_longer: Mean answer chars rose on haiku (470->505 inline, 404->530 conditional) and fell slightly on opus (770->780 / 737->744, flat). Explaining a refusal costs more words than asserting a ratio, on the weaker model.

the_rule._the_rule_under_test: results/2026-09-21-shape-replication.json _the_rule: semantics handle interpretation, classification, prevention and refusal; recipes are needed only for derived numbers.
the_rule.what_this_run_says: STRONG SUPPORT, and it repairs the contradiction the first Q2 run raised. That run reported prevention failing 0 of 60 with semantics present, which looked like a counterexample to the rule. It was not: the semantics needed were ABSENT, and the semantics present were actively misleading. Supply the right sentence and prevention goes to 59 of 60 with no recipe and no server-side computation. The rule survives; the first Q2 file's reading of this question should be read alongside this file.

caveats: n=10 per cell, 60 runs, ONE question, ONE sitting, immediately after a deploy.

This is NOT a controlled test of conditional pruning. Both arms ship the new sentence on this record, so the arm comparison here only confirms that pruning still costs nothing; it cannot show a pruning cost.

The sentence was written by the same party that wrote the question's ground_truth, and it states the same distinction in similar words. That is close to teaching to the test: the result shows the arms can USE a correct sentence when it is present, not that they would infer the distinction themselves.

The ep1 Paris Proof line remains in the block. A reader might reasonably say the block now contains one line inviting a comparison and another forbidding it, and that 59 of 60 chose the latter. Whether that is robust guidance or a resolved contradiction is not something 60 runs can settle.
Effectively saturated at 59 of 60, so benchmark-trap can no longer separate these two arms. It is now a regression test, not a discriminator.
The one miss and the 'invalid vs merely indicative' boundary that produced it is a judgment call of mine, applied consistently but resting on one run.
Token deltas are self-reported by the harness and come from a single sitting.
SIX arms changed, so prior results in results/ are not comparable on ep1/ep2/berekend questions — see the_comparability_warning.
The production finding was established from ONE live call to the Duurzaam server on one address. The alert text is quoted verbatim; no broader audit of that server was done.
still_outstanding: Q2's cross-record-comparison half. Now testable via metered-vs-model (Middenwetering 1, NEN 7120), where the new sentence IS pruned. Not run.
Re-measuring gas-estimate and total-vs-per-m2 after this block change, since all six prose arms moved.
The production Duurzaam server's Paris Proof alert — see the_production_finding. Needs an MCPSER ticket and a decision on whether to drop or reword it.

Whether removing the ep1<->70 line as well would change anything, now that the counter-sentence is present. That is the second half of the fix open-questions.md described, and it is deliberately not done.
